content: where are the newnjobs in the tracker

**Short answer: the newest jobs are rows 61–76, dated 14–20 October. Nothing newer exists — the drain found 0 new on 21–22 Oct.**

**Where they are in the sheet:**
- Rows 3–76: **Not Applied** (74)
- Rows 77–94: **Applied** (18)
- Rows 95–123: **Rejected** (29)
- Newest block, rows 61–76, is the tail of Not Applied — **Verkada (20 Oct)** is the single newest, then KnowBe4 (19 Oct), Shell (18 Oct).

**Why the drain added nothing.** From the search's own reconciliation on one batch: 16 roles found → **7 already tracked**, **5 rejected** (clearance / prior experience / closed), **3 held back**, **1 new candidate** (G-Research, which was already in the tracker at row 66). Across all 13 batches that nets to zero.

**The part worth your attention — 3 roles are being held back, not added.** They sit in "review-only" because the pipeline could not verify they are still open, so they never reach the tracker:

- **Apple** — Information Security Internship (London)
  `https://jobs.apple.com/en-gb/details/20068717171-2114/information-security-internship`
  (link as logged: `jobs.apple.com/en-gb/details/200687171-2114/information-security-internship`)
- **Revolut** — Internship Programme 2027: Information Security Engineer (Operations)
  `https://www.revolut.com/careers/position/fdab4dd9-1610-432a-b8ab-c984a15a54c5/`
- **PA Consulting** — 2027 Summer Internship – Digital (Digital Trust & Cyber Security), London
  `https://jobs.smartrecruiters.com/PAConsulting/744000156517180-2027-summer-internship-digital-digital-trust-cyber-security-london`

These are the closest thing to "new jobs" right now, and they are **not** in your tracker.

**One thing I want to flag, but not assert.** The rejection reasons have nonsense evidence attached — e.g. "clearance/citizenship required: **sc**, security clearance", and "prior experience required: **to a full background check. Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to**". Those look like mis-parsed fragments of the JD, not real requirements. That could mean real roles are being wrongly rejected. I have not verified any of them, so I'm calling it a suspicion, not a cause.

**Two questions:**
1. Want me to fetch those 3 JDs and add them if they're genuinely open?
2. The eligibility rejections — want me to audit whether they're real?

Stopped. No work in flight — I've made no changes since my last report.

**Current state, factually:**
- Tracker unchanged at **121 rows** (74 Not Applied / 18 Applied / 29 Rejected).
- Last commit `6a5df1774` — pushed, nothing uncommitted from me except files I didn't touch (`career-ops/linkedin_publish.py`, `remote-queue/logs/queue.log`).
- No background processes running from my side.
- The drain finished earlier with 0 new roles.

Standing by for your next instruction.

Investigation complete. **The pipeline is not failing to find roles. It finds them and throws every one away at a single gate.**

**The chain, with evidence at each step (last UK run, 21 Oct):**

1. **1,587 roles discovered** → prefilter keeps **219** → semantic review **219** → **72 accepted by DeepSeek**.
2. For each accepted role the pipeline tries to fetch the job page to confirm it is still open. It uses **plain `urllib` — no browser** (`jd_fetcher.py:141`), and the run records `browser_used: false`.
3. **Only 33 of 1,587 candidates ever get job-description text** (`jd_gap: with_job_description_text: 33, without: 1,554`). With no fetch, the fetcher returns `{"state":"UNKNOWN","evidence":"job not fetched"}` (`jd_fetcher.py:118`).
4. The eligibility gate rejects any role whose availability is not proven OPEN (`pipeline.py:932`).
5. Result: **71 of 72 rejected — every single one for `current vacancy availability not verified OPEN`.** The one survivor was already in the tracker → **0 tracker candidates**.

**The roles being discarded are exactly the ones you want.** From the rejected list: PA Consulting 2027 Graduate – Digital Trust & Cyber, Experian Junior Information Security Officer, NHS England Junior Threat Intelligence Analyst, WHSmith Junior Cyber Security Analyst, Financial Ombudsman Junior Cyber Security Analyst, Tencent Cyber Security Intern. All real. All thrown away as "unverified".

**And a second, independent failure on the 22:30 nightly run:**

```
semantic provider: "none"   model: "deterministic-title-policy-v1"
limitation: "deepseek answered but produced no usable classifications"
deepseek_attempt: requests 68, every error = "Insufficient Balance"
codex escalation: requested false — "disabled by the caller"
```

So on that run the model reviewer never ran at all: **your DeepSeek account is out of credit**, the deterministic fallback was used instead, its output failed the contract guard, and Codex escalation was switched off so nothing rescued it.

**Same root cause explains my 2-hour scan.** The 3 roles it held back — Apple, Revolut, PA Consulting — were held for "availability unverified". Identical gate.

**Verified vs inferred, since this matters:**
- **Verified:** DeepSeek balance errors (68 requests); Codex escalation disabled; 71/72 rejected on the availability reason; 33/1,587 JD texts; browserless fetch; the gate and the UNKNOWN default.
- **Inference, well-supported but not proven page-by-page:** that JS-rendered ATS pages (Workday, SmartRecruiters, LinkedIn) are why the browserless fetch yields no positive OPEN evidence. The fetcher does try an ATS-API fallback, so I can't yet say every page fails for that reason.

**This is also when it stopped.** Tracker candidates per run were 1–5 through 12 Oct; since 16 Oct they are 0 or 1.

**Three fixes, in order of impact:**
1. **Top up DeepSeek** — without it the nightly semantic stage is dead. This is your call, it needs account access.
2. **Re-enable Codex escalation** — it's a config flag currently set off by the caller.
3. **The availability gate is the structural one.** Either give the verifier a JS-capable fetch, or let a discovered, plausible role be added marked *unverified* instead of silently discarded. Right now the gate demands proof the verifier can't produce, so the answer is always zero.

I've changed nothing. Which do you want me to take on?
